projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The sustained high device count (17–20) with rapid fluctuations during a weekday afternoon strongly suggests the children are hosting friends or streaming, with devices roaming between Wi-Fi zones. This aligns with normal after-school activity, but the fluctuation pattern warrants a quick check to rule out unauthorized network access.

The presence signal shows 17-21 active mobile devices with rapid fluctuations, which is unusually high for a typical Monday afternoon with two school-aged children. This pattern strongly suggests guests or a gathering, but warrants a quick confirmation from Steve to rule out unexpected visitors or device anomalies.

The late-night jump to 21 connected devices, paired with zero camera motion and no dog activity, confirms the spike is localized to stationary IoT or background syncs rather than household movement. Combined with Steve’s 3.7h sleep versus Roxanne’s 11.7h, this points to an isolated personal sleep disruption rather than a shared household event, ruling out security concerns but underscoring Steve’s elevated fatigue risk for the morning.

The sustained high mobile device count at 3 AM, paired with zero camera/dog activity and Steve’s short sleep, indicates stationary devices rather than active presence, with Steve likely awake using his phone while the rest of the household remains asleep.

The persistent 18–20 mobile devices at 1:21 AM, paired with zero camera/dog activity and Steve’s severely truncated sleep, strongly suggests the children are likely still awake with multiple devices in their rooms, indicating a late-night screen time pattern that may be contributing to household sleep disruption ahead of the school week.
Steve slept only 3.71h last night. May be a rough morning — heads up.

The sustained 18–20 connected devices combined with zero camera motion and no dog activity over four hours strongly suggests a quiet, stationary gathering or a network glitch miscounting IoT devices as mobile; this matters because it confirms the household is likely settled but warrants a quick verification to rule out a connectivity anomaly or unaccounted guests.

The sustained 18–20 connected devices alongside zero camera motion and no dog activity for four hours strongly indicates a stationary, low-light gathering (likely a movie or gaming night) or Wi-Fi presence overcounting background IoT devices. This is likely benign but warrants a quick check to confirm cameras are active and the household is settled.

The sustained 18–20 connected devices indicates a gathering, but the complete absence of camera motion and dog activity over four hours suggests guests are either in a camera-blind zone, the cameras are disabled, or it’s a very quiet movie/game night. This warrants a quick check to ensure cameras are functioning and the household is comfortable.

The sustained 15–20 connected devices paired with zero camera motion and no dog activity over a four-hour Sunday evening strongly suggests the house may be unoccupied or the Wi-Fi presence detection is malfunctioning, as active children and dogs would typically generate movement. This discrepancy warrants verification to rule out a forgotten departure or network glitch before assuming normal evening routines.
